hooks.text: This dry lake is three miles long, and nobody drew the lines across it.
hooks.title: 3 MILE DRY LAKE

hooks.text: Why do straight tracks cross a dry lake that gets three inches of rain?
hooks.title: 3 INCHES OF RAIN

hooks.text: On this dry lake, rocks up to three hundred twenty kilograms leave tracks.
hooks.title: 320 KG ROCKS

beats.text: This dry lake is three miles long, and nobody drew the lines across it.
So what draws lines on a dry lake?
Rocks here weigh up to three hundred twenty kilograms.
From orbit, it's flat dried clay, walled in by mountains.
Central Park would fit inside it.
Those rocks are sailing stones. They travel across the clay.
They leave long racetrack imprints. Those are the lines.
People have documented this since nineteen forty eight.
Next target: hundreds of desert figures, found by drones. Follow for the next scan. Orbi out.

draft.description: Racetrack Playa is a dry lake in Death Valley National Park, California, where sailing stones weighing up to 320 kg travel across the clay and leave linear tracks. The phenomenon has been documented since 1948.
